sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle

announcements.name: Real-time (inline) Data Loss Prevention for Foundry
announcements.shortDescription: Security admins can configure DLP policies in Purview that block prompts containing sensitive information from reaching the LLM, using out-of-box or custom-defined sensitive data sets.
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft is introducing Realtime, or inline, Data Loss Prevention for prompts as part of the integration between Microsoft Foundry and Purview, enabled with the toggle of a button in the Foundry control plane. Security administrators can set up a DLP policy in Purview that triggers when an end user passes sensitive information into the LLMs, using either out-of-box sets that are part of Purview or custom-defined sets defined by the organization. When the Purview policy kicks in real-time, that particular prompt is blocked from entering the LLM or AI, preventing AI from learning on the organization's sensitive information.

announcements.name: Foundry–Purview integration toggle with non-PII insights
announcements.shortDescription: Enabling the toggle in the Foundry control plane lets admins set up inline DLP and surfaces Foundry-specific, non-PII data security posture insights for a subscription.
announcements.longDescription: Within the Foundry control plane, a Purview integration toggle has been introduced; once enabled, Purview admins in the Purview portal can start setting up inline DLP policies for prompts. Enabling the toggle also surfaces Foundry-specific, high-level insights from Purview for that particular subscription, covering all the AI apps and agents built within it. This information is all non-PII, so Foundry admins—who may not be security admins—get a bird's eye view of the data security posture without seeing PII-related information, helping connect the loop between security and Foundry admins.

announcements.name: Purview SDK integrated into the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can embed Purview compliance and data protection middleware directly into a custom agent's runtime with roughly 15-20 lines of code.
announcements.longDescription: The Purview SDK is now directly integrated into the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK, allowing developers to embed Purview compliance and data protection controls right into their agent runtime so the same enterprise-grade governance that protects Copilots extends to any custom agent. For pro developers building custom AI with Agent Framework SDK—whether with Langchain, OpenAI, Semantic Kernel, or any other framework—a Purview policy middleware can be added to the agent's workflow pipeline to intercept prompts and responses and enforce tenant security policies configured in Purview. Microsoft provides samples on GitHub in C#, Python, and Node.js, and the integration takes roughly 15 to 20 lines of code at max.

announcements.name: Insider Risk Management support for agent-driven activity
announcements.shortDescription: IRM now tracks agent-triggered policy matches, generating alerts with full context just as it has for user-driven activity.
announcements.longDescription: Insider Risk Management (IRM), the solution within Purview, can now track and list risks for agent-driven activity in addition to the user-driven activity it previously supported. When an agent triggers a policy match, IRM generates an alert and provides a full picture to the security team, just as it did for user-risk-triggered policy matches. The alert detail shows the specific agent involved, the user who triggered the interaction, the risk severity, and the sequence of activities—including what data the agent accessed, whether sensitive content was present in prompts or responses, and whether any DLP policies were matched—helping security teams assess whether it is a real threat or a false positive.

announcements.name: Azure AI Foundry evaluation results synced into Compliance Manager
announcements.shortDescription: Eval results and agent test status are automatically synced into Purview for associated agents.
announcements.longDescription: Within the Compliance Manager solution in Purview, evaluation results from Azure AI Foundry are automatically synced into Purview for the associated agents. The eval test status of the agents is updated accordingly, as shown in the solution.

announcements.name: Data Security for Local Agents
announcements.shortDescription: Discover, Protect, and Investigate pillars extend DSPM, DLP, and IRM to agents running on developer machines and endpoints, introduced at Build for managed agents with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.
announcements.longDescription: Introducing Data Security for Local Agents, which extends Purview's protection to agents running locally—such as coding assistants in IDEs, automation on laptops, and tools on endpoints the organization does not fully control—that can access files, credentials, and source code that never touch the cloud. The same three pillars used for DSPM for AI in cloud apply here: Discover, Protect, and Investigate, mapping to the lifecycle of managing risk around local agents. Discover uses DSPM to inventory every agent in the environment, Protect brings data loss prevention to the local agent layer so the same DLP policies used for cloud agents extend to local ones with no separate configuration, and Investigate provides the ability to look into activity when something looks off.
